vocab.definition: the % of reactant mass that becomes the useful product.
the product you actually want to make.
a product that is not wanted.
uses fewer resources and makes less waste.

misconceptions.wrong: Atom economy and yield are the same.
misconceptions.right: Atom economy is about efficiency; yield is about amount.

misconceptions.wrong: Use only the wanted product's atoms on the bottom.
misconceptions.right: Bottom line is the total Mᵣ of ALL products.

misconceptions.wrong: A high yield means a high atom economy.
misconceptions.right: They are independent of each other.

infoPanels.title: ATOM ECONOMY
formulaLines: atom economy = Mᵣ of useful productMᵣ of all products × 100

questions.text: State what is meant by atom economy. [1 mark]
CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O. Calculate the atom economy for Cu. (Cu=64, H₂O=18) [3 marks]
Explain why a reaction with only one product has 100% atom economy. [1 mark]
Explain why high atom economy is good for the environment. [2 marks]
Complete the sentence using the word bank. [2 marks]
questions.secondaryText: Atom economy = (Mᵣ of ______ product ÷ Mᵣ of ______ products) × 100.

questions.text: Suggest what a company could do with a valuable by-product. [1 mark]

footer.tip: Atom economy compares the wanted product's mass with the mass of ALL products.
footer.thinkPrompt: Why might a reaction with low atom economy still be used in industry?
